clauses.reason: The order commands "I hereby approve said amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended" under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. The command approves amendments whose text is not in the order and modifies the previous approval so that it covers the code as amended; it depends on section 3 in the same way as the original approval. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6922 (signed December 15, 1934) recites that the Federal Alcohol Control Administration submitted the amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry with its report, and that notice and a hearing were given, then commands "I hereby approve said amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended". The text of the amendments is not in the order. It states no period, condition, "until" date, exception or provisional approval, so no own-terms end applies. The command depends wholly on section 3 of Title I (approval of a code as amended), and under the reviewed shared analysis its first end is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for action completed while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5). Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after the repeal.
